findings.claim: The framing omits the lowest-risk option: no browser engine at all — manual paste-out/paste-back by the user (human-in-the-loop relay) plus the existing agy/CLI/API paths — which would serve one-off consults without building automation, distribution, or signing infrastructure.

evidence.observation: Brief motivates engine from labs that 'answer only in the browser' and jumps to driving web chat UI through Chrome; no manual-relay or do-nothing alternative is scoped.
A user copy-pasting the pack into their own tab and pasting the reply back needs no extension, relay, sandbox, or catalogue, so it dominates on ToS and maintenance cost for infrequent use.

findings.remedy: Add an explicit Option 0 (manual relay, possibly tool-assisted staging of pack/reply files) with a decision rule for when automation volume justifies the engine.
findings.trigger: Deciding to build the engine before pricing the manual alternative that carries zero automation-ToS exposure for the product.
findings.verification: Time one manual grok.com consult from a staged pack file and compare its cost against the estimated engine build plus per-site adapter maintenance.

findings.claim: Neither the brief nor the roadmap requires per-adapter informed consent to the user's own account risk (suspension, quota loss, subscription termination) before an adapter is enabled, leaving the heaviest cost on the least-informed party.

evidence.observation: Boundary places site-terms responsibility on the adapter author/user but specifies no consent surface, risk disclosure, or per-site ToS attestation at enable time.
Enable path is described only as user enables per site at human cadence with rate limits; no warning or attestation step is listed.

findings.remedy: Require the enable flow to show the site, the automation-relevant ToS clause link as supplied by the adapter author, and an explicit 'I accept the account risk' confirmation recorded in telemetry as consent, not content.
findings.trigger: A user enables a reference or third-party adapter for a site whose terms forbid automation and loses the account or quota.
findings.verification: Walk the enable flow in the design doc and check for a mandatory risk-disclosure plus attestation step before any adapter can send text.

findings.claim: The signing and revocation model is unspecified: who may sign, how keys are distributed and rotated, and how a compromised or ToS-violating adapter is revoked and blocked from running disable the catalogue safety story.

evidence.observation: Catalogue promises signatures and opt-in updates with the xelixir lands-disabled rule, but names no signer, trust root, key distribution, or revocation mechanism.
Without revocation, a retired/bad adapter entry remains runnable from cache, so the rating/retirement loop in Q5 cannot actually retire anything in the field.

findings.remedy: Specify pointers-and-hashes catalogue, named signers, a revocation list checked before each run, and cached-adapter expiry; keep all adapter bytes out of the product channel.
findings.trigger: A signed adapter is compromised or a site forbids its automation after the catalogue has listed it.
findings.verification: Inspect the catalogue format spec for signer identity, hash algorithm, revocation endpoint, and offline/stale-cache behavior.

reply_markdown:
Challenge first: the brief asks *how* to automate web chats, not *whether*. Unlisted options: (0) no engine — user pastes pack in, pastes reply back; (a) per-site CLI/API where one exists (agy covers the Gemini case); (b) OS-level accessibility driver instead of extension/CDP; (c) single-vendor spike (grok-only) to test value before a frame. To choose I would need: consults/month needing browser-only models, agy-vs-web answer overlap, one manual-relay timing, and counsel's view on catalogue/signing exposure.

**Q1 — Boundary.** Ship: engine, host API, manifest/catalogue *format*, signing/verification and revocation, sample adapter for a fictional/test page only. Never ship: site DOM selectors, default-enabled adapters, screenshots/docs naming forbidden-site targets, hosted adapter bytes, or usefulness copy promoting them. Precedents: userscript managers (engine + no bundled scripts, takedown on notice), Greasemonkey/Tampermonkey wording ('user scripts are user responsibility; check site terms'), 1Password-style BYOS ('your session, your vault'). Catalogue lists pointers + hashes + signer + ToS-attestation, never code.

**Q2 — Shape.** Safest order: extension content-script JS adapter behind a deny-by-default host API (chat-tab origin only, no cookies, no other tabs, no network) beats CDP/Playwright (full-browser capability, credential-adjacent) and beats WASM-first (WASM still needs the same JS shim for DOM, so the shim *is* the boundary; sign JS equally). Minimal contract: `start_thread`, `send_turn(text)->turn_id`, `read_turn(turn_id)->{state: streaming|done|blocked|error, text}`, `limits()->{max_chars, turns/day}`, plus `adapter_id/version` and a failure enum. Drop `attach` (no use case named). Prove against grok + one generic textarea site; defer Gemini until agy-overlap is measured.

**Q3 — Detection/abuse.** Add: no headless, visible tab must stay foreground, inter-turn jitter, per-adapter daily caps, stop wordlist (captcha/verify/rate/login-wall/interstitial → abort + mark `blocked`), no CAPTCHA solving or DOM cloaking, consent receipt per enable, and a public abuse-contact + takedown path. Log every turn locally.

**Q4 — Quality.** Mark browser replies `weight: provisional`, route only in panels until per-(adapter,version) win-rate clears a bar; per-adapter pack budget (grok small: ~2–4k tokens, pack slicer truncates periphery first); prefer site-thread continuation, stateless re-send only as fallback, and record which was used.

**Q5 — Telemetry/distribution.** Fields: adapter_id, version, site_hash (not plaintext), outcome class (ok/refused/blocked/error/truncated), turn count, repair flag, consent flag. Catalogue = signed pointers + hashes, user-supplied bytes, explicit enable, revocation list, cache expiry. Retire by (id,version)+outcome, never by id alone.

**Q6 — Order / not-build.** Build: (1) manual-relay + consent wording + one grok spike; (2) host API + contract + revocation design; (3) telemetry/outcome fields. Do NOT build: hosted adapter bytes, WASM toolchain, Gemini adapter, attach, PowerShell parity, or auto-updates — until the spike proves value.

## Requested checks
RC1: Time one manual grok.com pack→reply round-trip from a staged file; observe wall-clock and turn cost (needs browser read-only; 30 min). Settles finding #1.
RC2: Walk the enable-flow mock and confirm a mandatory ToS-risk attestation step exists (needs design doc read-only; 15 min). Settles finding #2.
RC3: Inspect catalogue spec for signer, hash algo, revocation check, and cache expiry (needs spec read-only; 20 min). Settles finding #3.
verdict_reason: Framing needs a no-engine baseline, consent, and revocation answers before any automation shape is accepted.
